title: Dedicated shapes benchmark results (raw runs + baselines)
content:
SHEET: Dedicated shapes benchmark results (raw runs + baselines)
Owner: Vanessa Ortiz (Fleet Capacity)
Last updated: 2025-02-21

Purpose
- Source-of-truth for benchmark runs used to set Dedicated tier throughput thresholds and apply safety factors.
- Includes raw runs (by shape/model/scenario), observed variance notes, and recommended “guarantee baselines” (what we can safely contract as sustained throughput).

Measurement notes (please read)
- Metric focus: sustained effective OUTPUT tokens/sec at the deployment boundary (gateway), aggregated over a fixed window.
- Windowing used for these runs: 10 min run, exclude first 60s warmup; compute rate over remaining 9 min; report p50/p95 across 30s sub-windows.
- Traffic pattern: closed-loop (constant concurrency) unless otherwise specified.
- Scenario families below assume typical production prompt-length mixes; details included in Scenario column.
- Exclusions not represented here: planned maintenance, customer-induced 4xx/5xx, downstream dependency failures.
- Runtime: Redwood inference runtime w/ continuous batching enabled; KV cache on; prefix caching off unless explicitly noted.

How to use this sheet
1) Pick shape + model family closest to customer workload.
2) Pick scenario that matches input/output length distribution + streaming behavior.
3) Use “Recommended guarantee baseline” (already includes safety factor + supply caveats), not the best raw run.

Notes on variance / outliers
- Region variance:
  - eu-west-1 L4 hosts currently show ~7–10% lower tps vs us-east-1 (CPU sku + kernel config differences). Action: Fleet to align host profile or bake region factor into guarantees.
- Host/network issues:
  - R-2025-01-27-01 flagged as NIC firmware-related drops; keep as a reminder that “SLO is platform end-to-end,” but exclude from baseline stats.
- MIG:
  - MIG run included only to quantify penalty. Dedicated tiers should assume no-MIG for guarantee shapes unless we explicitly define MIG tiers (not in scope).
- Long-context:
  - longctx-v1 is a different operating regime; decode tps is not comparable. Tier guarantees must specify context-length distribution assumptions.

Scenario definitions (quick)
- chat-mix-v1: input tokens p50~640 / p95~1600; output tokens p50~220 / p95~420; 70% streaming; mixed system prompts; closed-loop concurrency.
- longctx-v1: input tokens p50~2400 / p95~6000; output tokens p50~180 / p95~360; 70% streaming.
- burst-test-v1: same as chat-mix-v1 but open-loop arrivals w/ burst factor 2.0 every 60s; measures throttling/overload behavior.
- embed-v1: embedding requests input p50~96 / p95~160; output ~0; report reqps.

=== Tab: Baselines + recommended guarantee (includes safety factors) ===
Interpretation rules
- Baseline value used: median of “clean” runs for that shape/model/scenario (or single best available run if only one), using eff_out_tps_p95 as stability anchor.
- Safety factor (SF) applied to baseline p95 to derive recommended contractual guarantee.
- SF rationale: covers region/host variability, workload drift within stated assumptions, and oncall mitigations that may temporarily reduce throughput.

Recommended tier mapping (draft, for discussion w/ Product)
- Standard (small model tier): L4-1x, L40S-1x; guarantees based on chat-mix-v1 only.
- Performance (70B baseline): A100-80-2x; optional A100-8x NVLink for high concurrency.
- Premium (70B high throughput): H100-80-1x/2x as default; H100-8x NVLink where available.

Open questions / follow-ups (infra)
- Region normalization: do we enforce identical host profiles per region for Dedicated, or bake region-specific guarantee tables?
- NVLink node scheduling: need explicit reservation rules so “8x-nvlink” shapes don’t silently land on non-NVLink equivalents.
- Burst handling: burst-test-v1 suggests we need clear policy on when throttling is “expected behavior” vs SLO miss.

Change log
- 2025-02-21: Added H100-2x + Mixtral run; added burst-test-v1 row; updated SF for H100-8x from 0.84→0.86 based on lower observed variance in reruns.
- 2025-02-05: Added eu-west-1 L4 run; added MIG penalty row.
